Guests can also enjoy the serene waterfront setting of Jumeirah Mina Al Salam and the secluded Arabian houses of Jumeirah Dar Al Masyaf. Together, they form a one-of-a-kind destination rooted in Arabian luxury hospitality. d: The International University of Science & Technology in Kuwait (IUK) is a newly established private university in Kuwait, with a new Campus located in the heart of Kuwait near the Avenues Mall. Fully accredited by the Private Universities Council (PUC), the University offers a wide range of academic programs in three Colleges; namely: College of Engineering, College of Business Administration, and College of Arts. In addition to the academic programs, the IUK has established the University Foundation Program (UFP) that offers English and Math foundation programs. The IUK is looking for dynamic full-time faculty members who are passionate about teaching, and contributing to the development of a vibrant and successful learning environment for students.

The Department of Communication Sciences and Disorder at IUK invites applications for a full-time faculty position at the rank of Assistant/Associate Professor. The department seeks a specialist with a strong foundation in the biological and clinical bases of communication who can teach both the scientific and the applied components of the undergraduate program.

The successful candidate will teach courses on the anatomical, physiological, and neurological bases of speech, language, and hearing, as well as courses on hearing loss and its management and on the principles and procedures of clinical practice. The candidate will help students connect foundational science with clinical reasoning and prepare them for supervised clinical work.

Faculty members at IUK are expected to deliver high-quality teaching, maintain an active research agenda, and contribute to academic and community service. The successful candidate will work closely with the Head of Department, the Dean of the College, and colleagues to advance the mission of the department and the College. The teaching load is 12 credit hours per week. In addition to teaching, faculty members maintain regular office hours, advise students, contribute to curriculum development, and take part in the University's professional development activities.
q: A Ph.D. in Speech-Language Pathology / Speech and Language Therapy; or
A Ph.D. in Communication Sciences; or
A Ph.D. in Allied Health Sciences.
The degree must be awarded by a reputable and recognized university.
A minimum of three years of university-level teaching experience in communication sciences and disorders or a closely related field.
Clinical experience in speech-language pathology, speech and language therapy, or audiology.
Experience in clinical supervision or in preparing students for clinical placements is preferred.
A record of research and publication appropriate to the rank.
Experience teaching in a multicultural environment and supporting students with diverse learning needs, including students with special needs.
Ability to explain anatomical, neurological, and auditory concepts clearly using visual, digital, and hands-on teaching tools.
Familiarity with standard clinical assessment and intervention procedures in speech, language, and hearing.
Proficiency in learning management systems and e-learning tools.
Commitment to ethical and evidence-based practice.
Ability to work collaboratively within a team.
Good organizational and time management skills.
A passion for teaching and mentoring students.
r: Teach the anatomical, physiological, and neurological bases of speech, language, and hearing, as well as hearing loss and aural rehabilitation.
Teach clinical methods and prepare students for clinical practice, including supervising practicum where required.
Contribute to the development and review of courses, clinical components, and program learning outcomes.
Conduct and publish research in communication sciences and disorders or a related field.
Advise and mentor students, and maintain regular office hours.
Serve on department, College, and University committees, and support seminars, conferences, and community events.
Follow the University's bylaws, regulations, and quality assurance requirements.
